tips.comment: You've only got to glance at the card to see how little this lot win, so in-form CROWD QUAKE looks the most obvious choice. Turned over as an odds-on last time out, but still looks well in on the handicapper, and connections are clearly trying to make hay while this one is in the mood.
United Force could be worth a shot as he returned from a short break to a third last month and drops 1 lb, which puts him 1 lb below the mark when last winning here in July.
Cheek pieces will help today, hoping the step up in trip will help him this afternoon. Will have to show stamina to place or win.
A newcomer out of Camelot from the Watson yard to a winning half-sister and Group 3 winner Lightning Moon. All have gone well on debut.

Not beaten far when runner-up at Windsor on handicap debut earlier this month, coming back from a six and a half months break. Will strip fitter for that race and won't be over-burdened by the 1 lb increase.
Rossa has only had the leg up on this horse once and he won on him. Looks fairly well handicapped and has dropped a few classes since his last run.

Coolree did well at Beverley to win by over a length. Although up 4 lbs for that, his last win last May was off today's mark. If it was not for the expected soft going, I would have gone for a win but EW 4P.
Had a valid excuse last time and could bounce back here at decent odds. Worth a small EW bet in a competitive heat.
If there were 3 genuine places available (there aren't in most places), I'd nap this one. Has done nothing over the trip, and the turf here last time seemed to suit. Jockey is competent.
Could be suited by this drop in trip after finishing runner-up over a mile at Kempton 2 weeks ago. Remains on the same mark.

The forecast ground on the soft side will be ideal for this selection, who receives weight all around. Has a competent jockey on board and is back down to close to its last winning handicap mark, and this track should suit.
Solana Rose ran in a Listed race at York first time out and finished well in 6th place after having to wait for a gap and should win in this lesser company at Ripon.
Amber Honey won for the first time at the seventh attempt at Wolverhampton last week. He won comfortably there by 3.75 lengths and looks to have a great chance of overcoming the 7lbs penalty.
Heartened, a 3-year-old bay filly. Very poor 2-year-old last season but kept in training. Best run was last time out when beaten only 5 lengths. Down 2lb for that run, could be a nice each way price.
Improved rapidly over the last few months under his yard. Likes this track and has a strong trainer/jockey combination. I still think he has room to improve and is the one to beat today.
He came 2nd at Newcastle in November and then was 5/13 last month at Haydock after a 5-month rest. He should be ready to improve upon that run and go well today.

First start for new yard. Last run 33 days ago was a 4/12, finishing a shoulder behind 3rd, with the front 2 now rated mid-70s and low-80s respectively. Was similar going then and has a favorable draw here with 5 lbs being taken off by the jockey. Has a good chance here.
Beat a neck when runner-up over a mile and a quarter here 11 days ago. He is a former course and distance winner and should appreciate this drop back to a mile.

Only 2-44 but is generally quite consistent at this lowly level and has returned with a pair of solid 2nds at Redcar and Catterick this spring. Not one for maximum faith given his win record but should be in the mix once again.

Tends to improve on second or third race after a break, but still run well at Thirsk after a 72-day rest to take 2nd of thirteen nearly two weeks ago. 2nd here last year on soft ground, and won it back in 2023 on good ground. Lots to like.
Kept on well when winning over Nottingham's extended mile on the 10th of May and should appreciate this step up in trip. Made stable debut that day and likely more to come.
Let's Dream won at Chester in a C2 when last out when returning from a break. I always expect more when second up, and although up 4 lbs for that, he is still not top weight in this drop to C3.

Let's hope we Touch The Moon with this George Scott runner. He has had a decent time in the Middle East before returning to the UK. He raced freely last time. The yard is putting cheekpieces on today, and if they help, he could certainly run a big race from the front and be involved in the finish here if he runs his usual game race.

FIRST VIEW still looks feasibly treated for a turf handicap. A spell in Meydan through our winter can help an older type revive and this eight year old would likely have needed his comeback sighter. Sharper now potentially seen to best effect today he rates the value play.

The yard is going better now than it was a few weeks back, and the stable jockey is booked for the first time on this unexposed horse. This is the first turf run since the horse switched yards, and we might see a little more of the horse's true potential now off a 7 lb lower mark than the mark he was originally given in handicaps just 2 starts ago. His 2nd on the AW in a novice race makes him comfortably an 80+ horse for me, so this mark of 73 should see him be competitive.
Cloaks Of Gold was a decent C4 third on debut a couple of weeks ago. I would expect more now, second up after wind surgery, while dropping to C5 at the same trip on AW debut.
After 3 wins in a row, this horse disappointed when 8th at Newmarket. But that race was much better than this, and he should be taking this for Marco Botti, who's been amongst the winners.

Decent distance for Rogue Soldier, and I think he will like the trip better than his last run. Hasn't shown the form of last year, but this could be the time he shows his return to more consistent running. Worth an each-way gamble at this price.
Dreambird Dolly can grab 2nd place here showing potential when runner up at Brighton over this minimum trip on penultimate start. That form will see the selection go close.

Sometimes you get a gut feeling about a dodgy favorite, and this is one such time. The short-priced one hacked up on Tapeta, and today's surface is different. Plus, my selection is potentially still well treated after a consistent string of efforts and has decent form at this track/surface.

40% strike rate over C&D, finishing just over 1L behind the winner 31 days ago over C&D also. Proven over this trip and at this class, runs into a very strong favorite who seems to be ahead of the handicapper. I still expect Smith to be thereabouts, and if the race doesn't go how the favorite wants it, I believe Smith will be there to steal his thunder.
A beaten favourite over a mile and three quarters at Wolverhampton last time out and will come on for 2 runs this last month following a 6 month break with the step up in trip of appeal.

ONESTEPTWOSTEPS has been given every chance by the handicapper and it is noticed that this low-mileage eight year old's best effort was on Polytrack over a middle-distance suggesting this more extreme test wold suit. A sole entry for a shrewd dual-purpose trainer and maybe the stable are having a punt.

Unplaced in her only start last season, Polygram improved to finish 4th on her seasonal debut at Kempton last month and was then beaten just 0.75 lengths at Newcastle on 2nd May. There were 4 lengths back to the 3rd, and the winner was just denied a follow-up at Wolverhampton two days ago. So the form looks strong, and she can go one better here.
Hasn't won for a while but slipping down the weights as a result and returned with a decent 3rd at Ripon earlier this month. A step forward from that should put him firmly in the mix this evening.

Back down to a winning mark of 55, having won off this mark in August 2024 at Musselburgh. Will strip fitter for 2 runs in the last 5 weeks following a 6-month break and welcome the slight drop in trip, having raced over the extended mile at Nottingham on the 9th of May.

LOCKDOWN LASS is clearly well treated and may be capable of a revival with the yard in such fine form. She is a mature experienced type who has a solid enough back-profile relative to racing in this company and she merits a marke check.

This just strikes me as one of those weak-looking class six affairs where you can't make a case for the shorter prices with any real conviction. Therefore, you can't really rule anything out too readily either. A key plus for GOING UNDERGROUND here, that negates the poor run of form, is the fact he was only a length and a half behind current favorite Martin's Brig at the end of last month, and he's now on four-pound better terms. He was unlucky in that race, and if back in that mood, could get involved.

Brummell is a 4 year old sprinter likely to go through the ratings this season if the form shown on debut is anything to go by. The nap impressed with a good turn of foot in the final furlong when winning at Beverley.
Hasn't won for a while but is generally a consistent performer and ran well when 4th in a decent race at Ascot last time. Down another lb and should be capable of striking soon.

We can draw a line in the horse's poor run last time out when slowly away and racing over too short a trip. This looks much more her bag. She was very impressive when winning at this trip by 6 lengths on debut, and this mark of just 76 looks a winnable one given the horse's unexposed profile. She was sent off at odds-on when 3rd on her last start last year, but the 2 in front of her are high 80s horses. So the fact she was fancied to beat them strongly suggests that she could well go close here.

Water Of Leith was well fancied last time and just got beat with luck in running. Here tonight, the Jim Goldie runner could well gain compensation. It should certainly be involved in the finish if running a similar race to its last one.
Brought a long way for this race by Ralph Beckett, drops in grade after finishing runner-up over a mile and a quarter in a Class 2 at Newmarket last time out and holds an entry in the Irish Derby.

The trainer is looking good recently. Recent form doesn't look great, but Tootsie is dropping a grade here today, so could well capitalise against weaker competition. Could be the restart that's needed.

Showed potential in debut run when a useful 3rd of 9 at Newmarket last August and then gained valuable experience at this course when 3rd of 6 last August. Was competitive LTO in handicap debut when 4th of 11 at Newmarket earlier this month. Mark remains unchanged but has a chance if further improvements are made.

Trained at Newmarket by John Gosden, the very well-bred Wicked could be thrown in here. On breeding, Wicked should have won at least a maiden by now. However, he may be a horse that just needs a little time to grow into himself.

Second last time, steady improvement. Travelled really well and pulled clear of the rest. Beaten favorite, good jockey on board. Should be there in the closing stages. Great each way bet at 8/1. Nap Each Way.

Trawlerman is a solid second-best pick, boasting excellent form over similar going and distance. Though not at his best in Dubai, his Group-level performances at Ascot last year, including a second in the Gold Cup, suggest he’s a major player if able to dictate from the front. Hood also brings out his best.

Coltrane has not been great June-Oct last year but did win last May when second up after a break. He returned from a break last month, showing improvement when second. I would expect more now, second up, while keeping Oisin in the saddle.

Expensive Breeze Up purchase First Legion justified that optimism by pouncing late at York over six furlongs. It should cope with the rise in class and the drop in distance at Sandown, drawn well in stall 2 in this Listed five-furlong sprint.

Took a big step forward when scoring decisively at Kempton over 6f, confirming promise from Ascot debut. Though this is her turf debut and a stronger contest, she’s progressive, has a sharp turn of foot, and Buick is a notable booking. She could easily surprise some better-fancied rivals if transferring her form to grass.
Eskimo Pie can go close in this competitive sprint after finishing 2nd on debut at Newmarket over 6f. The drop back to the minimum trip will suit much better.
Two wins from two with wins at Bath and Salisbury. Have to respect the form at this price. Still looks to have bags of improvement. Can't overlook this horse. Likes the going.
Trainer Ed Walker is very sweet on the chances this evening of stable star Almaqam. He ran well enough here 34 days ago on his season reappearance.

Unbeaten in four starts, including a Group 3 win at Longchamp, Ombudsman sets a strong standard with proven versatility across ground conditions and distances. His perfect record over this trip and on similar going speaks volumes, and with Ryan Moore booked and the Gosden team handling his progression, he’s clearly the one they all have to beat despite the penalty.

A mixed bunch of results on all weather and on turf, and obviously prefers an artificial track. But has run on heavy ground at Longchamp and then good to soft at Chester when putting in bad performances, and has only run on decent ground when last in the Derby at Epsom. Given a chance here as he is an improving type and looked very good on season debut at Kempton and the choice of William Buick.

Won at Newmarket over 7f and twice at Chelmsford over 8f when having his first run of the season. Was second in Listed at Ascot on good over 10f on last run, which was 250 days ago. But four of the last five winners of this race had over 200 days away from the course, and the tip is getting 3lb weight off several rivals.

Ancient Wisdom is the selection here in what is a fine looking Brigadier Gerard Stakes. Last year's Derby eighth ran a good race from the front to finish second (Almaqam third) to Al Aasy over course and distance last time. Group 1 winner as a 2yo who added a Group 3 to his tally over 1m5f at Newmarket last year. Both Charlie Appleby (SR 45%) runners appeal. William Buick opts for Military Order so James Doyle rides Ancient Wisdom who offers a little more value at a double figure price. Tactics will be interesting. This 4yo Dubawi colt has a big future still.

The stable is just starting to kick into life. Based on the novice win at Wolves, beating Docklands and conceding 9 lbs, this horse may have more to give this season after being gelded over the winter. It has winning form here, and the comeback 3rd here in the Bet365 Mile was a step in the right direction.
Persica is clearly on the up when winning a G3 after a short break last month. While unable to follow up in a G1 a couple of weeks ago, I think the return to G3 could see him bounce back EW.
Surrey Shadow. Lightly raced 4-year-old grey gelding. Ran well at Doncaster last time out, rated 87. Up a pound for that effort, he should run his race here.
This up-to-now disappointing type (this season) might benefit from the hopefully significant booking of R. Moore, who has decent stats for Hughes' yard. A drop of rain may aid the cause.

Lightly raced and highly promising, Golden Ocean ended last season with back-to-back wins over 1 mile, including a victory over the reopposing Quadruple. Proven on today's ground and distance, and now under the care of an accomplished UK yard, she looks to have scope for further improvement. With Oisin Murphy booked and solid form under her belt, she is a standout candidate if ready on return.
Showed promise with her previous yard but bred to do much better. The switch to this stable could unlock further improvement, and she's well drawn. Big player.
Big reappearance figure last year off a similar break. Is now 3lb lower than last win, which can only help him at Sandown. Trainer in good form. Can go close here.

The Class 3 Whitsun Cup handicap is a competitive affair although nothing exceptional stands out. Jack Channon trained Arkhalia Flynn, a 4yo by Ulysses out of a Dutch Art mare, returns for the season. Three wins and three second place finishes from ten runs suggest a tough sort. George Bass (SR 16%) rides. Drawn in stall 8 and allotted 8 stone 12 pounds here, still looking well handicapped on a mark of 84. 12-1 price looks value for a stable that does particularly well with its handicappers at the mile trip (Johan springs to mind).
Denied the hat-trick when upped in trip to a mile and a half at Newcastle last month and could benefit from this drop in trip.

De Temps En Temps won his second bumper at Fairyhouse in January but disappointed when only 4th as the odds-on favorite back there on his hurdles debut in February. That, though, looked like a good race, and it could be that he is also better on good ground, having finished second on it in a point. He looks the most likely winner here.

If Ifallgoeswell for this C Byrne runner, it should certainly be involved in the finish. It was fourth last time over hurdles and is lightly raced, so could still be improving. It could be involved in the finish if continuing to improve.

OCEAN OF MERCY has a signficant long absemnce to overcome , but a trainer who knows how to get one ready and no doubt he has some smart lines of back-from. The market can likely privide us with further clues in maiden hurdles , so maybe these overnight odds are value.

The model I run suggests The Man's Room should win this race. This result has been driven by The Man's Room having by far the highest RPR of the 12 runners here. Looks well treated on the weights and is right near the bottom of the order for this 2m trip. This is the first race in 115 days, and so race fitness might be the reason for the higher price. The model indicates a 'low stake' reading, which translates to a 0.75pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

The model I run suggests Crowsatedappletart can win this one. This result has been driven by Crowsatedappletart having the second highest RPR of this 18-runner field, but a comparatively low official ranking. This leaves him carrying less weight compared to the majority of the field. Crowsatedappletart is a previous course winner and distance winner and looks to get the CD winner tag here today. A good second place 7 days ago and he's been wheeled out here in quick succession to try and take advantage of the form. Darragh O'Keeffe on board picks up the reins. The model issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Onefortheditch won twice last summer at Kilbeggan off 86 and at Cork off 92. She continued to run well and was placed over 2m5f here at Limerick off 102 in November. She returned from a break when only 8th at Cork earlier this month but should progress from that and looks a good each-way bet with 5 places on offer.

O'BON PARDON runs with the yard among the recent winners and an upwardly mobile still 3lb claiming conditional jockey abard. That boosts the chances of this young potential handicap improver and the blinkers fitted can be read as a sign of intent today.
I can't back against the market leader here as Devils Angel was a good looking winner last time out at Navan, and a run like that would be good enough here too.

VERIFIED would ap[ear to have a chance on rating s in thos Claimer category race. Still a young horse as a four year old capable of better and he is well drawn for early track position today. A sharpener behind him shoud have help set this sprinter straight and he appeals.

The model I run suggests Emily Love should win this race. Emily Love has by far the highest RPR of this larger 18-horse race and comes here with form figures of 3332-2. That most recent second came only 19 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4. This is predominantly driven by the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

STILY stayed on in the manner of a young horse coming to hand likely better suited by today's distance. He should also step forward second-up for this out of season campaign and that could put him in a better place than some in opposition.

The model I run suggests an upset from That's All. This result has been driven by That's All having a comparatively high RPR compared to the rest of this large 18-runner field. Has got a relatively low official ranking compared to the other runners and subsequently is given less weight to carry around this 2m 3f trip. John Shinnick on board claims a further 3 lbs and leaves That's All carrying weight firmly close to the low order. Last ran only 19 days ago, so race fitness should not be a concern. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, predominantly as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

IS THAT LOVE brings course and distance winning form , so it is interesting that this nine year old returns to this venue on the back of an improved effort at Rosscommon. She was formerly a much better higher rated racer , so with signs oif a revival in a weak handicap she should be competitive.

It’s been a nightmare trying to keep up with the weather this past week, but I’m almost certain we’re in for a deterioration in the going with the forecast of heavy overnight rain here in County Meath. That, in my humble opinion, wouldn’t do the chances of the unexposed four-year-old filly HAPPY HENRY any harm. Trained by Willie McCreery, she made her turf debut 36 days ago at Gowran Park over 7f on heavy ground. While finishing 7th of 15 and beaten 5¼ lengths, she actually shaped quite nicely travelling well one furlong out before fading late.
This daughter of BUNGLE INTHEJUNGLE has been dropped 3lbs since that run and is knocked back to 6f here, which looks a positive move. A big plus is that top jockey Billy Lee retains the ride. He knows his way around Fairyhouse, boasting a 21.05% win strike rate at the track over the past year. He also has a 30.17% place strike rate when teaming up with this trainer in the same period.
Should the ground soften further, I certainly wouldn’t be discounting this unexposed filly dropped back in trip. Conditions might just tilt things in her favour.

First reserve, so no certainty to start. Likeable sort who is 1 lb out of the handicap here. Showed some early speed and faded when 11th of 19 behind Devil's Angel at Navan recently. Entitled to come on for that recent outing, the first in five months. Won 2 of 22 starts on turf, formerly with Denis Hogan and now with Paul Flynn. Likely to go in at a decent price at some stage, I think.

Forty Kay is a 5-year-old daughter of No Risk at All ex Calakanga, who traces back to two great broodmares, namely Sweet Mimosa by Le Levanstell and Feemoss by Ballymoss. She makes her racecourse debut here in this mares-only bumper, where she'll be ridden by Mr. P.W. Mullins for his father W.P. Mullins, in the colors of the Blueblood Racing Club. Runners here with form may not be too strong, and it may be open to a newcomer to come to the fore on this occasion. I make my selection my Nap of the day.

The Willie Mullins forecast favorite doesn't look anything special on paper, so the selection is the Emmet Mullins-trained Barra Rua. She is related to numerous winners, including Coney Island, and going back to the prolific winners Rhinestone Cowboy and Wichita Lineman. The trainer has an exceptional 25% record in bumpers over the last 5 years, and top amateur jockey John Gleeson takes the ride.

The model I run suggests an upset for Sing My Story. This result has been driven by Sing My Story having the highest RPR of this 14-runner field. All horses step out carrying the same initial weight, and Mr. Aherne on board relieves a further 7 lbs claiming. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Jessica Harrington horses have been coming back into form gradually. This Too Darn Hot filly ran well, showing early pace each time, in two decent maidens last year. Good chance of having progressed from that at home in the interim. Has kind of showed her colours now so may be up for this on third maiden start. Nathan Crosse rides.
Got off the mark at the fifth attempt when winning a nineteen horse race at Down Royal earlier this month. The 7 lbs increase might not be enough to stop him going in again here.

The model I run suggests Tir Og can win this one. Tir Og lines up here with the joint highest RPR of this larger 18-runner race but has an official ranking that leaves him well treated in the weights. There is 9 lbs less to the current market favorite and over a stone to the top weight, which can be significant over this 2m 3f trip. Good second 19 days ago and looks to build on the good form here. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

LADY NIGHTINGALE is a mare who has often shown up well through qualifying and she could well be seen to good effect freshened up now racing from a career-low hurdles mark . She has a talented 5lb claiming conditional aboard which could be a pointer towards expectation and she appeals.

Klassman is still a maiden after 14 starts but was placed in 4 of his last 6. He was pulled up last time at Ballinrobe, but the 3 miles trip on yielding ground was obviously too far for him. Back at 2m3f on good ground, he looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.

There isn’t an awful lot to latch onto at the prices here, but one that has caught my eye is trainer Donncha Duggan’s six-year-old gelding BALLYKINLAR. There are a few reasons for interest. Firstly, we see this charge making his handicap bow on completely different ground than he’s encountered in his maiden and bumper runs. Being a son of IRISH WELLS, he should relish the faster surface expected today at Limerick.
Secondly, it’s worth noting that this lad has contested stronger maiden races than he faces here, which may explain why the handicapper has allotted him a relatively high mark for a newcomer to handicaps. That experience might just prove valuable in this lesser field.
Most interestingly, Duggan holds a 100% strike rate in handicaps granted, from just one runner - but it hints that the yard doesn’t waste these opportunities lightly.
At 20/1, I’m happy to take a tentative each-way stab. The market may be underestimating him, and if the ground brings about improvement, he could outrun those odds. Certainly not a stake your mortgage kind of punt but enough to prick my interest.

Solid efforts, especially over the 7f trip, since joining Ade McGuinness from Natalia Lupini. By Twilight Son out of a Paco Boy mare whose progeny have won races. Yet to score in ten starts but went down by just a neck on one occasion at Dundalk. Drop back to 7f from 1 mile gives this 3yo filly more of a chance. 3lbs out of the handicap proper. Julian Pietropaolo claims 3lbs. Might be well in at these weights on best form.

NATIVE DREAM makes handicap debut and could prove well treated for his first start in this sphere. He has four hurdles sighters behind him now and with an experienced rider booked apparently no need to claim from top weight his chance looks realistic.

The model suggests an upset here from Rideau Canal. This result has been driven by Rideau Canal having the highest RPR in this 18-runner field. This horse also has the second lowest official ranking of the entire field, leaving him well treated on weights. Rideau Canal steps out carrying the second lowest weight of the entire field. Form leaves a lot to be desired, but last ran 34 days ago and race fitness shouldn't be a concern. The model indicates a 'very low' stake, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

ALTO SAX is a ride for a bang-in-form apprentice jockey and Keithen Kennedy rode this four year old when showing up well at odds latest. He is a Saxon Warrior-sired four year old who returns to the scene of his course and distance win and should prove hard to contain.
Ok - goes well for a young female jockey - tick, course specialist - tick, coming here off a decent last time effort - tick, won't mind any rain - tick. That's enough reasons to have a decent bet.

1st reserve BARRYS ROCK seldom runs a bad race here at Fairyhouse. He somehow keeps his best form for here. Was placed 4 times here the last 2 seasons off higher marks than this. Has run well fresh here too when 2nd here off a winter break 2 seasons back. That’s all the good stuff. The bad stuff is he’s 10 and still a maiden, and others bring way more form to the table. But at 33/1, I’ll have a wild swing.
